tagline.text: A Catholic pilgrimage site with a 98 m statue of Mary overlooking Batangas Bay

location.label: Location
location.text: Sitio Montemaria, Barangay Pagkilatan, Batangas City

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱900–1,800 (day trip by public transport from Manila, per person)

children.text: Montemaria Shrine is a Catholic pilgrimage site on a headland in Barangay Pagkilatan, Batangas City. A roughly 98 m statue of Mary, "Mother of All Asia," a cross on its crown, chapels, a view deck, and a glass bridge draw pilgrims and ordinary travelers alike.
Montemaria Shrine is a Catholic pilgrimage site on a headland in Barangay Pagkilatan, about
40 minutes
by road southwest of Batangas City proper. From a hilltop roughly
above sea level, it looks west over Batangas Bay, and on clear days the sea stretches toward Tingloy, Verde Island, and the eastern coast of Mindoro. From Manila it is about
3–4 hours
away when traffic is light, so a day trip is feasible.
The heart of the shrine is a statue of the Virgin Mary known as "Mother of All Asia – Tower of Peace." From the base of the tower to the cross on top it stands about

(given as 98.15 m), and it is known as the tallest statue of the Virgin Mary in the world and the tallest structure of its kind in the Philippines. The structure is hollow, with chapels, rooms, and a view deck inside. The statue stands on a globe with arms outstretched, and its head carries a crown of twelve stars, representing the twelve apostles, topped by a cross.

The project began in 2014 and the tower was completed in 2021, tied to the 500th anniversary of Christianity in the Philippines. It was first started by the foundation of Father Fernando Suarez; the Mandanas family, who had donated the land, later took it over and donated the land to the Archdiocese of Lipa. For that reason construction is still going on across the complex, and a hotel, a marine museum, and a rosary trekking trail are planned.

The shrine has two sides as a destination. One is the chapels, rosary garden, and Way of the Cross used by pilgrims who come for Mass and prayer, and this area is free to enter. The other is a set of paid attractions: the tower view deck, the glass bridge over the cliff called the "Miracle Walk," a mirror deck, a maze, and a 9D cinema. Because a place of worship and tourist attractions share the same site, it matters to dress and behave in a way that suits the setting.

blocks.title: The Mother of All Asia statue and cross

children.text: The roughly
statue rising above the headland can be seen even from the waters of Batangas Bay. A large cross stands on top, and after dark the lights come on, giving the shrine a different mood from the daytime.
This view deck is reached by elevator inside the statue. Admission is about
, children under 7 enter free, and seniors get a discount. You can see the sea toward Batangas Bay, Tingloy, and Verde Island, and on the deck a white cross stands under a glass canopy.
This glass-floored walkway extends toward the cliff, about
long and about
above the water. It opened to the public in January 2026 and costs about
. The walk takes about
20 minutes
and is not for anyone afraid of heights.

blocks.title: St. John Paul II Chapel and Santo Niño Chapel

children.text: Mass is held on weekends and public holidays in these two chapels below the tower. The Santo Niño Chapel was the first building on the site and is said to be modeled on a church in Prague. Entry is free, and clothing that covers the shoulders and knees is required.

blocks.title: Way of the Cross and rosary garden

children.text: This free pilgrimage area follows the slope of the hill. There is little shade, so walk it in the morning or toward sunset rather than at midday.

blocks.title: Mirror deck, rainbow glass ladder, and dream maze

children.text: These attractions are good for photos. The mirror deck costs about
, the rainbow glass ladder about
, and the dream maze about
. Prices have changed often, so confirm on site.
A short film experience in moving seats, about
. It is a good way to get out of the heat when you are traveling with children.

When the sun sets over Batangas Bay in the west, the whole headland turns red, and after dark the statue is lit up. However, public transport back ends early, so it is easier to enjoy with your own vehicle.

Arrive at the parking lot and take photos in front of the chapels and the statue near the entrance. The path from the parking lot to the view deck entrance is uphill, so the earlier you start, the cooler it is.
On a Saturday or Sunday you can attend the
Mass in the chapel. Mass times differ by day, so see the notes below.
Go up the tower view deck and look out over Batangas Bay. The morning is quiet before lines build up.
Have a simple lunch at the restaurant inside the tower. Cash only.
Walk the Way of the Cross and rosary garden and look around the souvenir shop.
If you are going back by public transport, leave by this time. Jeepneys become scarce late in the afternoon.
Go up the tower view deck first.
Walk the Miracle Walk, then look around the mirror deck and the rainbow glass ladder.
Eat lunch at the restaurant inside the tower, and rest in a chapel or the 9D cinema during the hottest hours.
Walk the Way of the Cross while waiting for sunset.
See the lit statue, then head down by your own vehicle or a tricycle you have booked.
The full-day route suits you if you have a car or rental car, or have arranged a ride back in advance. If you rely on public transport alone, it is hard to stay until sunset.
Head south on SLEX, take the STAR Tollway, and exit at Batangas City.
After the exit, follow the "Montemaria" signs to Barangay Pagkilatan. Map apps are sometimes wrong on village roads, so watch the signs too.
The one-way toll for a sedan is about
, and from Makati or BGC the drive takes about
2–2.5 hours
. Parking at the shrine is about
for a car, about
for a motorcycle, and about
for a bus.

items.title: From Manila by bus and jeepney

children.text: From Cubao or Buendia, take a JAM Liner or DLTB bus to the Batangas Grand Terminal. The fare is about
and the ride takes about
2.5–3 hours
From the terminal, take a jeepney or multicab through Batangas City to SM City Batangas. Each ride costs about
. Direct rides from the terminal to SM are rare.
At the SM City Batangas jeepney terminal, board a jeepney toward Ilijan and tell the driver you are getting off at "Montemaria." The fare is about
and the ride takes about
30–40 minutes
Jeepneys back become fewer late in the afternoon. It is safest to leave by about
; if you miss them, look into a chartered tricycle (reported at around ₱500) or a ride-hailing app, but the signal can be weak, so download an offline map.
From central Batangas City to the shrine is about
40 minutes
by car.
If you are going without a car, withdraw cash in advance at SM City Batangas. The shrine reportedly does not accept cards or e-wallets.

In the dry season, November–May, the skies are clear and the sea views and sunsets are at their best. From March to May, however, the midday sun is strong and there is little shade on the hill, so early morning or late afternoon is better.

The busiest times are Holy Week, the Christmas season, and December 8, the Feast of the Immaculate Conception. The parking lot fills early on those days, so arrive before 8:30 AM or after 2:00 PM. Weekday mornings from 7 to 10 AM are quiet, and for pilgrims, the time before the first Mass on Sunday is good.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: The best time to visit, with good views and sunsets. Around December 8 it is crowded.
Visit in the early morning or toward sunset, and bring water and a hat.
Operation of the glass bridge and the view deck may change because of weather. On windy days, check on site.

There is no lodging within the shrine complex yet, and a hotel is only at the planning stage. If you want to stay overnight, hotels in Batangas City or around SM City Batangas are the usual choice. Many travelers combine the shrine with a beach resort such as Anilao or Laiya.
For food, use the restaurant on the 4th floor of the tower and the small eateries in the complex. Listed prices are around
for tapsilog (cured pork with egg and garlic rice) and
for pancit canton. All of them take cash only, so bring enough for admission and meals together. If you are spending a day here from Manila, budget about
for lunch.
Only cash is accepted inside the shrine. Cards and e-wallets such as GCash are not taken, so withdraw cash in advance at an ATM at SM City Batangas.
When entering a chapel, avoid sleeveless tops, shorts, short skirts, and revealing clothing. A light shawl or windbreaker is useful both for the wind on the view deck and for entering chapels.
From the parking lot to the view deck entrance the way is uphill with little shade. If anyone in your group is weak in heat or on slopes, drop them off first and then park.
The Miracle Walk is not recommended for anyone afraid of heights. Lines can be long on weekends, so go early in the morning.

Mass is held several times on Saturdays from 8 AM to 3:30 PM and on Sundays from 7 AM. There are also reportedly Masses at 4 PM on the first Friday of each month and at 9 AM on the 8th of each month. Public holidays differ, so check the official Facebook announcements.
Drones may be flown only in open gardens and within line of sight, and must stay away from the statue's face and from worshippers at Mass. Pets are allowed only outdoors and on a leash.
Prices and hours have changed often, so check the latest announcements. The complex is still under construction, so some areas may be closed.
This is a place of worship, so keep quiet during Mass, and the glass bridge and view deck can close suddenly because of weather or safety checks.
Public transport becomes noticeably scarce from around
, so if you plan to stay until sunset, book a vehicle in advance.
Prices and hours differ by source. One listing says weekdays 7 AM–7 PM and weekends from 6 AM, while an older one says 8 AM–6 PM. Check before you go.

Weddings can reportedly no longer be held at the Santo Niño Chapel after May 2026 and must be booked at St. Michael the Archangel Parish in Ilijan. Wedding photo shoots are allowed, but there is a separate fee.
During Holy Week and on December 8, crowds and cars cause traffic jams and parking is hard to find.
Mobile signal can be weak on village roads. Bring an offline map and cash.
A port city about
40 minutes
by car from the shrine, and a base for lodging and transport.
The island you can see in the distance from the view deck, reachable by boat from Batangas port. It has diving and beaches.
A diving destination on the Mabini side, a good pairing with the shrine for a two-day trip.
A beach on Tingloy Island, in the direction of the islands visible from the shrine's view deck. It makes a good boat-trip getaway.
